text:
alex: Hey @sam @molly — pushed fixes for the concurrency edge case you called out in #4123. Also added a small load test and uploaded results. CI showed one flaky windows integration, everything else is green. Can you take a quick look when you have a minute? https://ci.redwood/in/4123/build/5678 :pray:
ci-bot: build #5678 (linux/mac) passed, windows flaky test re-run queued (triggered by alex).
sam: quick q — the loadtest uses 32 concurrent clients, is that representative for the canary workload? also can you paste the exact command you used to run it locally so i can reproduce?
alex: yep — 32 was our baseline for the canary profile. local command i ran:
```
python tools/run_loadtest.py --clients 32 --rps 200 --duration 60
```
results artifact: https://artifacts.redwood/loadtests/4123/loadtest-5678.json
molly: skimmed the results — p95 latency looks fine. one small nit: can you add a single-line note in tools/README.md about the default args you used so others can run the same baseline? otherwise looks good to me.
alex: done — added README line and a short comment in the test. also added a smoke assertion to catch the kv-cache edgecase you saw. pushed as fixup.
ci-bot: re-run triggered for build #5679 on alex's push — all checks passed ✅
sam: thanks, looks sensible now. LGTM from my side. if ops is fine with the canary window, go ahead and merge. :+1:
molly: :thumbsup: i'll schedule the canary at 10:30 PT and watch the dashboards.
alex: thanks both — i'll merge after the canary window and report back here if anything unexpected shows up.
